ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: “chasing the clod.” In the corpus it belongs to a recurrent animal comparison: “the lion bites the person; the hound chases the clod.” The phrase appears as an appraisal after exchanges and in admonitions such as “you must be a lion that bites the person; do not imitate the hound chasing the clod.” Related forms call people “mad dogs chasing the clod” and say “chasing the clod and tracking the scent does not yet make a good dog.”
